---
title: "Tutorial"
---

Earth2Studio.jl re-exports the `earth2studio` Python module and its submodules as `Py` objects. Anything you can do in Python you can do in Julia by calling into these objects via [PythonCall.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/PythonCall.jl).

## Exposed names

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Earth2Studio

earth2studio  # earth2studio
data          # earth2studio.data
models        # earth2studio.models  (use models.px and models.dx)
perturbation  # earth2studio.perturbation
io            # earth2studio.io
run           # earth2studio.run
statistics    # earth2studio.statistics
utils         # earth2studio.utils
```

Each is a `PythonCall.Py` reference — attribute access, calls, and conversions work the way they do in PythonCall.

## Calling into Python

### Data sources

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Earth2Studio
using PythonCall  # for pyimport, pyconvert, pylist, etc.

# Construct a data source
ds = data.ARCO()

# Call its __call__: ds(time, variables) -> xarray.DataArray
np = pyimport("numpy")
t  = np.array([np.datetime64("2024-01-01")])
arr = ds(t, pylist(["t2m", "u10m"]))
```

### Prognostic models

```{julia}
#| eval: false
# Each model class exposes load_default_package() and load_model()
pkg   = models.px.FCN.load_default_package()
model = models.px.FCN.load_model(pkg)
model.to("cuda")
```

### Diagnostic models

```{julia}
#| eval: false
pkg = models.dx.PrecipitationAFNO.load_default_package()
dx  = models.dx.PrecipitationAFNO.load_model(pkg)
```

### Workflows

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Dates, PythonCall

t = pyimport("numpy").array([pyimport("numpy").datetime64("2024-01-01")])
backend = io.ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")

# Deterministic
run.deterministic(t, 10, model, ds, backend)

# Ensemble
perturb = perturbation.SphericalGaussian()
run.ensemble(t, 10, 4, model, ds, backend, perturb; batch_size=4)

# Diagnostic
run.diagnostic(t, 10, model, dx, ds, backend)
```

### IO backends

```{julia}
#| eval: false
io.ZarrBackend("/tmp/out.zarr")
io.NetCDF4Backend("/tmp/out.nc")
io.AsyncZarrBackend("/tmp/out.zarr")
io.XarrayBackend()
io.KVBackend()
```

### Statistics

```{julia}
#| eval: false
m = statistics.rmse(reduction_dimensions=pylist([]))
m = statistics.acc(reduction_dimensions=pylist([]))
m = statistics.crps(ensemble_dimension="ensemble")
```

## Bringing results back to Julia

Use `PythonCall.pyconvert` to convert Python values to Julia. For arrays, `PyArray` gives a zero-copy view:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using PythonCall

# After a workflow run, an xarray Dataset / DataArray lives on the backend
xr_dataset = backend.root            # depends on backend type

# Convert a numpy array to a Julia array
a_jl = pyconvert(Array, xr_dataset["t2m"].values)

# Or a zero-copy view
a_view = PyArray(xr_dataset["t2m"].values)
```

Refer to the [PythonCall.jl documentation](https://juliapy.github.io/PythonCall.jl/stable/) for the complete set of conversion utilities, and to the [earth2studio docs](https://nvidia.github.io/earth2studio/) for the Python API itself.
